experiences.downstream_task: Alzheimer's disease detection using Cookie Theft picture-description task recordings
experiences.goal: Keep the spoken content and evaluate all methods to summarize what works for this task.
experiences.lesson: For Alzheimer's disease detection using the Cookie Theft task, Resyn (TTS resynthesis) is the best choice. Prosody retention is poor (pit_pcc=0.045), but its high intelligibility (WER=0.025, CER=0.0135) and naturalness (MOS=3.83) accompany the strongest anonymization result (EER=53.6, closest to the 50% target as characterized in this record) and almost unchanged downstream performance (BACC 0.754 vs. baseline 0.757). NeuralVC retains some prosody (pit_pcc=0.297), with lower intelligibility (WER=0.353), naturalness (MOS=1.88), and a recorded EER of 51.3. Among signal-processing methods, formant_spec offers the weakest protection (EER=14.8), despite reasonable intelligibility (WER=0.177). Pitch and formant_lpc provide modest protection (EER 31.2 and 36.1, respectively). For a task that depends on understanding speech and is sensitive to identity disclosure, Resyn removes acoustic identity cues while high-quality TTS preserves clinically usable information.

experiences.lesson: NeuralVC is the best choice for psychological crisis risk detection. Its EER is close to the 50% target (49.5%), and it retains prosody and emotion, keeping downstream BACC at 0.738 vs. the 0.765 baseline. Emotional similarity (emo=0.955) and SNR (40.4 dB) are also high. Resyn offers the strongest reported anonymization (EER=51.5%) and highest naturalness (MOS=2.22), but resynthesis reduces emotional similarity to 0.852, nearly eliminates prosodic correlation (pit_pcc≈0), and drops BACC to 0.633. Formant_spec and formant_lpc retain some prosody but leave substantial identity exposure (EER 18.7% and 22%). Formant_spec also has low BACC (0.676). Prefer NeuralVC for this task, which depends on fine-grained emotional prosody.

experiences.lesson: For picture-elicited story generation in ENNI, signal-processing methods preserve downstream performance best. Pitch gives the highest downstream BACC (0.831 vs. the 0.849 baseline) and an EER of 46.7%. Resyn attains an EER of 50% and the highest MOS (4.28), but BACC falls to 0.754 as resynthesis disrupts acoustic cues to prosody and narrative coherence. NeuralVC has BACC 0.81 and a high prosodic error (Pit_L1=11.9), despite EER 48.9%. Formant_lpc and formant_spec achieve BACC 0.824 and 0.822. Prefer a less disruptive signal-processing method such as pitch for this open-ended task. Consider Resyn or NeuralVC when anonymization is paramount and the downstream performance loss is acceptable.

experiences.lesson: For the Spanish cognitive assessment task in Ivanova, baseline BACC is 0.448. Among signal-processing methods, formant_lpc performs best (BACC=0.503, F1=0.476, EER=40.0%, MOS=1.25). Formant_spec and pitch fall below the baseline (BACC=0.421 and 0.396, respectively), and pitch has EER 36.7%. NeuralVC has BACC 0.399, EER 43.3%, and MOS 1.72. Resyn has BACC 0.396 and the EER closest to the 50% target (45.0%), with the highest MOS (3.22) and lowest WER (0.099). Its low prosodic correlation (pit_pcc=0.036) harms a task that relies on prosody. Formant_lpc offers the best privacy–utility balance for this task.

experiences.downstream_task: clinical speech dataset for depression detection
experiences.goal: Keep the spoken content and evaluate all methods to summarize what works for this task.
experiences.lesson: Resyn performs best for Mandarin depression detection on MODMA. Downstream BACC rises from 0.782 to 0.842, and Resyn has the lowest CER (0.04) and highest MOS (3.23), indicating that resynthesis retains useful clinical speech features. NeuralVC offers EER 44.5% but poor prosody retention (pit_pcc=0.07, pit_l1=5.06), with BACC below baseline (0.773). Pitch gives EER 56.7% and CER 0.204. Formant_lpc and formant_spec leave substantial identity exposure (EER 13.9% and 16.3%). Prefer Resyn when intelligibility, privacy, and clinically relevant speech features are all important.

experiences.lesson: For cognitive assessment on NCMMSC-AD, Resyn provides the best balance. Its BACC of 0.687 is slightly below the 0.709 baseline, while it combines high intelligibility (CER=0.048) and EER close to 50% (47.9%). Pitch gives EER 57.6%, high CER (0.404), and reduced downstream performance. NeuralVC preserves more prosodic structure (pit_pcc=0.128 vs. 0.012 for Resyn), but has EER 46.7% and CER 0.365. The formant methods give better intelligibility than some alternatives but expose identity (EER 14.7% and 19%). Prefer Resyn for cognitive assessment that requires strong anonymization and accurate verbal content, with some loss of prosodic fidelity.

experiences.lesson: Parkinson's disease detection requires a balance between anonymity and preservation of subtle pathological acoustic cues. Formant_lpc performs best among local waveform modifications. It has BACC 0.85, closest to baseline 0.862, and intermediate protection (EER=27.1%). NeuralVC has EER 48.1%, alters prosody (pit_pcc=0.315), and yields a still-usable BACC of 0.843. Resyn has the highest recorded privacy and naturalness (EER=48.6%, MOS=3.58), but resynthesis removes diagnostic acoustic cues and causes BACC to fall to 0.515. It is unsuitable here when detection depends on those cues.

experiences.lesson: Cleft-palate speech assessment trades off privacy (EER near 50%) against diagnostic accuracy (baseline BACC 0.699). Signal processing retains much of the diagnostic performance (BACC 0.64–0.69), but leaves identity exposed (EER 11.9%–34.9%). Resyn gives EER 44.0% and the highest MOS (2.49), but alters prosody (pit_pcc=0.004) and acoustics so much that BACC drops to 0.526. NeuralVC offers the best balance, with EER 48.8%, prosodic correlation 0.214, and BACC 0.641, about 0.06 below baseline and above the other strong-anonymization options. Its CER is high (0.241). Prosody and acoustic structure matter most for this clinical assessment.

experiences.lesson: Pathological-voice detection shows a privacy–accuracy trade-off. Signal processing retains acoustic cues and keeps BACC high (formant_spec=0.693 and pitch=0.665 vs. baseline 0.715), but offers weaker anonymity (respective EERs 24.2% and 42.2%). Resyn and NeuralVC reach EERs of 51.7% and 51%, near random guessing. Resyn has low prosodic correlation (pit_pcc=0.068) and BACC falls to 0.488, indicating major loss of diagnostic cues. NeuralVC retains some prosody (pit_pcc=0.443) and yields BACC 0.656. Prefer Resyn when privacy dominates, or NeuralVC to balance privacy and diagnosis. Signal processing retains the most downstream utility in this comparison.

experiences.lesson: For pathological-voice detection, pitch and formant_spec preserve original acoustic cues. Pitch BACC is 0.814 vs. the 0.807 baseline, while respective EERs are 43.8% and 22.1%. NeuralVC improves EER to 46% but degrades diagnostic cues (BACC=0.739). Resyn attains the best reported anonymity (EER=52.6%) and naturalness (MOS=3.24), but removes pathological cues and drops BACC to 0.489. Avoid full resynthesis when downstream detection remains important. Resyn offers strong anonymity when a major diagnostic performance loss is acceptable.

experiences.lesson: For pathological-voice detection, signal processing retains diagnostic acoustic cues (formant_lpc BACC 0.894, formant_spec 0.877, pitch 0.87). EERs of 23.4%, 20%, and 39.7%, respectively, indicate residual speaker identifiability. NeuralVC achieves EER 50%, but BACC falls to 0.83. Resyn has EER 49.3% and MOS 3.22, but full speech regeneration removes diagnostic cues and BACC falls to 0.473 vs. the 0.901 baseline. Prefer approaches that retain original acoustic details when downstream utility matters. High anonymity entails a substantial utility loss in this comparison.

experiences.lesson: Resyn is the best overall choice for detecting suicidal thoughts or behaviours on Suicide-YF. It gives BACC 0.663 vs. the 0.668 baseline and CER 0.02, preserving semantic information for classification. EER is 41.2%, indicating some residual identity cues. Pitch, formant_lpc, and formant_spec retain prosodic structure, but BACC falls to the 0.60–0.65 range. Formant_lpc exposes identity (EER=18%), and pitch reaches EER 52.3% with the lowest downstream performance. NeuralVC gives MOS 1.82 and EER 46.7%, but CER 0.336 and low prosodic correlation (pit_pcc=0.126) accompany lower BACC (0.629). Prefer TTS resynthesis when retaining verbal information is important for mental-health risk detection.

experiences.downstream_task: Distinguish healthy controls (HC) from patients with depression-related disorders (PT)
experiences.goal: Keep the spoken content and evaluate all methods to summarize what works for this task.
experiences.lesson: For classification of Italian depression-related disorders (PT) versus healthy controls (HC), baseline BACC is 0.853. Pitch, formant_lpc, and formant_spec yield BACC 0.852, 0.8, and 0.825, but EER 31.9%, 36.2%, and 17.7%, respectively, indicates substantial identity exposure. NeuralVC gives the highest anonymization result (EER=48.3%) with lower intelligibility (WER=0.258, CER=0.167), MOS 1.72, and reduced BACC (0.774). Resyn gives EER 43.1%, high intelligibility (WER=0.021, CER=0.012), MOS 2.44, and BACC 0.896, above baseline. Prefer Resyn when this clinical task requires privacy and accurate verbal content.

experiences.downstream_task: Distinguish healthy controls (HC) from patients with depression-related disorders (PT)
experiences.goal: Keep the spoken content and evaluate all methods to summarize what works for this task.
experiences.lesson: NeuralVC is the preferred method for depression detection on Androids-Corpus-R. Its EER of 50.9% is closest to the 50% target and BACC exceeds baseline (0.724 vs. 0.699), indicating preservation of useful pathological acoustic features. Resyn has EER 46% but BACC 0.516, consistent with loss of clinical cues during resynthesis. Signal processing preserves some prosodic structure but exposes more identity information (EER 23.2%–35.3%). Formant_spec reaches BACC 0.745. The historical assessment interprets that improvement as possible reliance on insufficiently anonymized speaker cues. Prefer NeuralVC when this task requires both strong anonymization and diagnostic utility.
